subject: always missing 1st line from input in the output

messages.author: 57059e469d052267
messages.subject: always missing 1st line from input in the output
parts:
Hi folks,

I seek some help with a problem that does not seem to go away - the 1st input line in my file never appear in my output.

I am trying to perform Fisher's Exact paired tests on an input file with multiple rows (one row for each protein) and multiple columns (multiple biological properties), and adjusting p-value using FDR.

For each row (or protein), I want to compare whether each of its properties is statistically more abundant than expected by just chance.
The amino acid residue counts (for single protein, and sum total of all proteins) are therefore used for this calculation.

I am attaching an example input file, and my R code thus far (with various variation commented out).

I'd like the output to contain the protein ID as well as CoDomain classification information (as 'A' or 'P'), followed by adjusted p-values for each property (14 columns) for a row, iterated over each of the input rows.

When I convert table to dataframe, I am always missing input line #1 from the output. 654 input lines, 653 output lines!!!!

When I do NOT convert read.table to dataframe, I get only < 600 lines in output, compared to input file with 654 data lines.

I've tried several variations of my R script, but I am not sure about where I am going wrong - read.table? or cat / output step? elsewhere?
I hope someone can help fix the bug in my R script and explain to me what I was doing wrong, so I wont make this same mistake again.

Thanks!
Anand

messages.author: 47ca46208a81ec5e
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: always missing 1st line from input in the output
parts:
Hi Anand,

I think your loop is okay, but the use of sink() might be the culprit. It looks like sink() works similarly to some of the graphics device functions, like pdf(). You open a path for your data to go, and then you close up that path after you’ve finished adding everything by bookending the sink() function call and the close() function call around the block of code that generates the output you want to save. 

If I take out all of your uses of sink() and close() and just add a single call to sink(outfile) immediately before the loop, and a call to close(outfile) immediately after the loop, then it looks like the complete output file is generated.

I think the problem before was that the first sink(outfile) function call came as the *final* step of the loop. So the things in the loop worked great, the first row of output was printed to the screen, and THEN the file was opened for input. So the first time any results were actually written to that file was after the 2nd iteration of the loop.

I don’t know how common it is to use sink() and close() in your domain. I’ve never used them, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t the right choice for you case. Another way to do this without using sink() and close() would be:

1) Create a storage data frame just before the loop:

d <- as.data.frame(matrix(0, nrow=r, ncol=16))

2) Put the output from each iteration of the loop into the appropriate row (do this right after you make the ‘out’ variable):

d[i, ] <- out # Put the ‘out’ variable into the ith row of the d data frame

3) Check your work by looking at the the top 6 rows of d *outside* the loop.

head(d)

4) Write the variable to a csv file:

write.csv(d, outfile, row.names=FALSE)



--
